name: CC Switch v4.0.17
body:
# CC Switch v4.0.17

本版本修复了 4.0.16 带来的两个问题，并改进了托盘快捷面板。轻量模式又能释放托盘面板占用的内存，Windows 上的 WebView2 进程能正常退出；Codex 进入路由时不会再还回一份早已过期的 ChatGPT 登录、卡在登录页。托盘面板在应用之间悬停时不再跳动，在高缩放和小屏幕的 Windows 上也能完整显示；额度条对齐了，并显示距重置还有多久，剩余余额标成绿色；Windows 上左键点托盘图标恢复为打开主界面。Hermes 的供应商标识和内置供应商重名时，表单会给出提醒。另外修复了 Windows 上退出后路由端口仍被占用、Codex 远程压缩的用量记成 0、同时勾选多个 MCP 服务器时有的丢失、只有地址的 MCP 服务器同步到 Hermes 和 OpenCode 后是空的、TOML 字符串里的弯引号被改掉、数据胶囊的 WebDAV 同步失败、macOS 把手输的 API Key 首字母改成大写、在便携版目录上安装 MSI 后仍被当成便携版等问题。4.0 完整的更新内容请见 [v4.0 发布说明](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v4.0.4-zh.md)。

**[English →](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v4.0.17-en.md) | [日本語版 →](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v4.0.17-ja.md)**

---

## 改进

**Hermes 的供应商标识和内置供应商重名时给出提醒**。Hermes 遇到和内置供应商同名的标识（如 `deepseek`、`openrouter`）会改用内置那家，要它自己的环境变量 Key，这张卡的地址和 Key 都不生效；4.0.16 只修了 MiniMax 两个预设（[#8538](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/8538)）。现在填的标识是 Hermes 内置供应商的标识时，输入框下方会提醒并建议改成 `cc-switch-<标识>`；已经添加、标识改不了的卡，会提示用别的标识重新添加。`kimi` 这类别名不受影响，也不会报。提醒不影响保存。

**托盘面板的额度显示**。各档额度的标签、进度条和重置时间排成整齐的三列，进度条起止对齐，也更长了；重置时间从具体日期改为「还剩多久」，例如「1天23小时后重置」。按量付费的剩余余额只把金额标成绿色，和供应商卡片一致；余额用完时仍显示警告色。

**Windows 上左键点托盘图标恢复为打开主界面**（[#8572](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/8572)）。右键弹出设置里选的托盘样式（面板或菜单）。macOS 不变，左右键都弹出所选样式。

## 修复

- **轻量模式下托盘面板一直占着内存**（[#8612](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8612)）。4.0.16 起托盘面板默认开启，它是单独的一个窗口，第一次弹出后只隐藏不关闭，进入轻量模式后 Windows 上的 WebView2 进程也不会退出。现在轻量模式下面板一收起就释放，下次点托盘图标再重新打开。
- **Codex 进入路由后卡在 ChatGPT 登录页**（[#8573](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8573)）。4.0.16 起，进入第三方路由时如果 `auth.json` 里没有登录，会还回最近收起的那份；这份登录可能是几个月前收起的、早已过期，Codex 桌面版拿着它反复刷新失败，每次进出路由又会被还回来。现在已过期的登录不再还回，仍留在暂存里，切回官方卡时照常还回。
- **托盘面板悬停时来回跳动，Windows 高缩放下显示不全**（[#8572](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/8572)、[#8595](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/8595)，[#8549](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8549)、[#8553](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8553)、[#8564](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8564)）。两栏高度改为以主面板为准，供应商多的列表在右栏里滚动，在应用之间悬停时行不会再挪到鼠标下面，只有一个应用时也不再留出大片空白。Windows 上按显示器的缩放比例换算尺寸，面板会收窄并限制在屏幕可用区域内，底部的「打开主窗口」和「退出」不会再被挤出去；挪到缩放不同的另一块屏幕后，第一次弹出也能正确显示。
- **Windows 上退出 CC Switch 后路由端口仍被占用，下次启动报 os error 10048**（[#8552](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8552)）。CC Switch 打开的终端和命令行工具继承了监听端口，CC Switch 退出后端口仍被它们占着，下次启动只能回到直连，直到重启电脑或换端口。现在这些子进程不再继承监听端口。
- **Codex 远程压缩的用量记成 0**（[#8479](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/8479)）。Codex 0.153 起，远程压缩的用量写在另一种记录里，以前没有读取，这些请求都按 0 计。现在会正常计入；升级前已经扫描过的记录保持原样。
- **同时勾选多个 MCP 服务器时，有的没写进配置文件**（[#8580](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8580)）。几次勾选同时写同一个配置文件时会互相覆盖，界面显示已启用，配置文件里却没有。现在会依次写入。
- **只有地址的 MCP 服务器同步到 Hermes 和 OpenCode 后是空的**（[#8579](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8579)）。在 JSON 模式里粘贴或通过深链接导入、只写了 `url` 没写 `type` 的服务器，以前被当成本地命令，同步后 Hermes 里只有 `enabled: true`，OpenCode 里命令为空，界面却显示同步成功。现在和 Codex 一样，有地址、没有命令的按远程服务器处理。
- **TOML 字符串里的弯引号（含中文引号）被改成直引号**（[#8559](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8559)）。为了兼容中文输入法，导入 MCP 和编辑 Codex 配置时会把弯引号转成直引号，以前连字符串里面的也一起转了，把 `"don’t"` 改成 `"don't"`，有的合法配置还会被拒绝。现在只转换用作字符串边界的引号，字符串里面的保持原样，用中文输入法直接输入引号仍然可以。
- **数据胶囊的 WebDAV 同步上传失败，返回 500**（[#8554](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8554)）。现在同步清单改用通用的文件类型上传，内容不变，新旧版本可以互相读取。S3 同步不受影响。
- **macOS 上手输的 API Key 首字母被自动改成大写。** 显示明文时，输入的 `sk-…` 可能被系统改成 `Sk-…` 保存下来，导致认证失败。现在这个输入框关闭了自动大写、自动更正和拼写检查。粘贴的 Key 不受影响。
- **在便携版目录上安装 MSI 后，仍被当成便携版，只能手动下载更新**（[#8529](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/pull/8529)，[#3132](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/3132)）。现在安装时会删掉目录里残留的便携版标记 `portable.ini`，安装后可以在应用内更新。卸载时不会删除这个文件。

## 升级说明

**数据库结构没有变化**，仍然是 20。

- Windows 上左键点托盘图标恢复为打开主界面（4.0.16 用面板样式时是弹出面板，菜单样式一直如此）；右键弹出「设置 → 通用 → 托盘样式」里选的样式。
- Codex 远程压缩的用量只从升级后读到的记录开始计入，升级前已经扫描过的不会补算。

---

## 致谢

感谢 @funkpopo（托盘面板的滚动与缩放）、@Chaoqi31（Codex 远程压缩用量）、@chonngyi（在便携版目录上安装 MSI）的贡献。

感谢 @SamPheng、@xinxinxiaoxin、@XinwangTao、@ramonmi、@Jdker22、@Geneslves、@Jinmoli、@nanfenggushi、@fereverlove、@hulkbig、@AngryBigCat、@QC2168 报告问题、提供复现信息和修复思路。

完整的技术细节请见 [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)。

name: v2.13.0 — Added the conversion-tracking skill (1.0.0). Setting up, auditing, verifying and fixing t…
body:
- Added the **`conversion-tracking`** skill (1.0.0). Setting up, auditing, verifying and fixing the path from a conversion on a website to Google Ads, Meta, GA4, LinkedIn, TikTok and Microsoft Ads, for lead generation and ecommerce. Gives an orphaned job a home. Analytics listed conversion tracking as a trigger without covering it, attribution routed pixels and CAPI to ads, and ads held one reference file. Built on one distinction, that lead gen has to infer success from a browser signal while ecommerce reads it from an order record. Nine references (how each form, booking and chat tool signals success, the complete browser-side path, the server-side options with prices, ecommerce platforms including Shopify's 26 Aug 2026 Additional Scripts removal, Google Ads, Meta, other platforms, the audit playbook, and why the numbers never match), 26 detection snippets (22 form and booking tools plus 4 universal patterns), importable GTM recipes merged by `scripts/build_recipe.py`, and 16 evals. Audit scoring follows the ads skill's audit guardrails, summarised inline. New skill = repo y release; total skills: 52. Contributed by Aaron Beashel (Converly ◆, a Verified Partner) and reviewed against the repo's partner-integrity bar before merge:
  - **Neutrality:** free and native paths first (browser Enhanced Conversions, Meta advanced matching, Google tag gateway, Meta CAPI Gateway, tool webhooks); a "when server-side matters less" section; the partner row matches the others in length and lists its tradeoffs; a free-tier row in the side-by-side; paid options surface at the delivery decision, not in every answer; the contributor's other tool (Attributer) is disclosed with alternatives; five neutrality evals (ids 17–21).
  - **Facts:** browser tags can send hashed email and phone; Meta dropped the AEM 8-event cap in May 2023; Microsoft has a Conversions API (self-serve token, still rolling out); LinkedIn dedup needs a shared `eventId`; Meta CAPI for CRM gates; Google tROAS vs tCPA minimums; conversion-adjustment windows; Shopify's 1 Oct 2026 script-tag change; the undercount stated as a 10–30% range rather than a universal 30%.
  - **Assets:** 18 detection snippets replaced with listeners that passed live checks on real forms, Jotform's now firing on the completion message its iframe and script embeds send, and Framer's confirming through Framer's own form request; every GTM recipe uses Tag Manager's import format, so Import Container accepts it; 10 drifted GTM recipes regenerated from their snippets, with `scripts/check_recipes.py` to keep them in sync; `build_recipe.py` validates every ID and substitutes safely (no JSON or JS injection) on Python 3.8+; every send tag requires consent (the Google Ads conversion tag `ad_storage` only); snippet success-signal types documented; four new tested detectors (Squarespace Forms, HubSpot Forms, Cal.com and Acuity Scheduling), for 26 in all.
  - **Repo fit:** operative rules in the description, a revops boundary, no cross-skill relative links, two audit checks restored from the retired ads reference.
- **Converly integration guide** filled in (capabilities, setup, operations); platform lift stats carry a holdout caveat.
- **analytics** (2.2.0 → 2.2.1): description drops the "conversion tracking" and "track conversions" triggers and hands getting conversions into ad platforms to conversion-tracking.
- **attribution** (1.1.5 → 1.1.6): pixels, CAPI and server-side conversion tracking now route to conversion-tracking (description, Boundaries, Related Skills, and the by-business-type tooling note).
- **ads** (2.6.1 → 2.6.2): conversion tracking pointers (routing table, Platform Setup, tracking setup line, google-ads-audit-checklist) now go to the conversion-tracking skill; description and Related Skills name it. `references/conversion-tracking.md` retired, its content carried into conversion-tracking's browser-side.md, audit-playbook.md and server-side.md.

name: v2.12.0 — New skill: link-building, for earning links and third-party mentions that lift rankings a…
body:
New skill: **link-building**, for earning links and third-party mentions that lift rankings and AI citations.

- **link-building** (new, 1.0.0): confirms links are the bottleneck with a page-level link gap before any outreach, then ranks tactics by effort and quality (unlinked mention reclamation, partner and integration pages, moved and broken links, "best X" list inclusion, resource pages, broken link replacement, editorial guest articles) and hands PR, podcasts, directories, reviews, and communities to their own skills. Every placement is judged for SEO authority and for whether AI engines cite the page, so mentions without links count. References cover tactic playbooks, prospecting and qualification with outreach templates and a tracker, and a risk policy built on Google's spam policies (updated 2026-08-28): paid placements carry rel=sponsored or nofollow, plus vendor vetting, manual actions, and when disavow is warranted. name: v0.6.8
body:
**ripwire 0.6.8: more complete first answers, and fewer false edges.** This release collects four batches of reviewed changes (trains 28 to 31). `--for` stops when its answer is
complete, `--callers` and `--callees` serve more rows whole, `--impact` of a type finds the code that uses it, and the call graph proves more receivers and hedges more
guesses, with the guesses labelled. The numbers below say what was measured, on what, and what each one does not show.

## Read this first
- Caches are rebuilt once. Every ingest cache and quality snapshot an earlier build wrote is refused and re-indexed on first run (parser version 206, cache version 36, snapshot scheme 22).
- Go: a method's id is now `file::Type::method`. Quality-baseline rows, `.ripwire_quality_acks` rows and `.ripwire_notes` pinned to a Go method stop matching: re-pin them (`--notes` lists an old note with `dangling="1"`; `--note-add` with the same target stores the new id).
- Scripts that read `next=`: on a cut `--callers` answer it is now the next page (the `--uses` follow-up moved to `uses_next=`); on a capped `--callees` page the `--expand` follow-up moved to `expand_next=`; on a `--for` answer with a body fold, `<sigs next=>` names the first skipped body and the signatures-only call moved to `sigs_next=`.
- `--for` with no `--token-budget` now stops when it is complete (a 7,500 B target, a 30,000 B guard that says when it fires); an explicit `--token-budget` is a soft target whose cuts stay recoverable through `next=`.
- Git: ripwire now pins repository-configured filter and diff programs to nothing for its own git commands (`--doctor` reports it). Files behind a repository-local filter (git-crypt, a per-repository LFS driver) are read as stored.
- `--quality-delta=A..B` under a memory limit can answer with the kinds it can decide and exit **6** (new) when that partial answer has no gating row; `--quality-kinds` (new) runs only the kinds you name.

## Measured: the same 173 questions, 0.6.5 then 0.6.7 then 0.6.8
Each answer is graded two ways: a **stricter** method (a rubric item counts only when the answer names the item's primary symbol, or at least two of its listed terms) and a **more lenient** one (any one listed term). A question counts as answered completely when its first answer covers the question's pre-written must-mention list. Only the first answer to each question counts.

| first answer complete, of 173 | 0.6.5 | 0.6.7 | 0.6.8* |
|---|---|---|---|
| stricter method | 50 (about 29%) | 83 (about 48%) | 98 (about 57%) |
| more lenient method | 78 | 109 | 127 |
| the 10 questions from one repository we set aside before any build for this release ran (stricter) | 2 | 5 | 6 |
| answers that claimed a wrong target (mechanical check against pre-listed wrong targets) | 3 | 0 | 0 |

\* The 0.6.8 column was measured on the train-28 build of 0.6.8, the first of the four batches. The later changes in this release (trains 29 to 31) were measured only on their own target questions, in the next section, and are not in these counts. A re-run on the final 0.6.8 build of the 29 questions the train-28 build had answered completely only by the more lenient method: 9 are now complete by the stricter method too, and none of the 29 lost a matched item (the other 144 questions were not re-run). Grading is mechanical and the same machine ran all three builds. A hand read for false claims covered a sample of the 0.6.7 and 0.6.8 answers; the 0.6.5 answers were barely read, so their false-claim count is a lower bound.

- Since 0.6.7, 15 questions got better and none got worse (stricter method), and the mechanical wrong-target check found no wrong-target answer in either build.
- By language (stricter method), 0.6.5 then 0.6.7 then 0.6.8: C 5, 12, 13; C++ 6, 9, 10; JavaScript/TypeScript 13, 20, 23; Python 12, 20, 21; Go 4, 6, 8; Ruby 3, 6, 10; Rust 5, 5, 7; Java 2, 5, 6.
- What it costs: the first answers to the 60 development questions total 356,443 B with 0.6.7 and 427,247 B with the 0.6.8 build measured here (+19.9%).
- Other tools: on the 120 of these questions that five other code-intelligence tools also answered (unnamed here; each at its version as of 2026-10-08; one of them covered 108 of the 120), those five answered 13 to 35 completely with the stricter method and 23 to 44 with the more lenient one, against ripwire's 66 and 89 on the same 120 (ripwire at the build described above). On the final 0.6.8 build, 7 of the 23 questions in this set that ripwire answered completely only by the more lenient method are now complete by the stricter one too, and one (fzf-02, in the table below) went the other way; the other 97 were not re-run. A named, complete comparison is planned for 0.7.0.
- How to read it. On an earlier 163-question round a hand read of the grader's output fell between the two methods (more lenient 99, stricter 75, hand read about 81 to 85), so treat the truth as between them. This is one round on our own questions, and it does not include trains 29 to 31.

## Later changes, measured on their own target rows only
Measured per change, on that change's target rows, not a full table. The rows differ per change and overlap, the base builds differ, so **do not add these up**. "Stricter" and "more lenient" are the two methods above.

| batch | change | rows measured | before, then after (items matched, or complete / not) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 29 | callers served whole up to 50 rows | ninja-06 `--callers=Stat` | stricter 2 of 6 items, then 6 of 6 (+270 B) |
| 29 | `--impact` of a type starts from the symbols that name it | tmux-10 `--impact=grid_cell`; hono-10 | 0 of 32 files, then 32 of 32 (1,341 to 6,141 B); 12 of 14, then 13 of 14 |
| 29 | minimum arity: an overload a call cannot reach is not listed | ninja `--callees=ParseDefault` | the unreachable second candidate is gone; stricter 8 of 8 before and after |
| 29 | Go receiver scope (#403); Rust standard-type member gate (#405) | fzf `--path` with qualified names; mdBook `--callers=iter` | "endpoint not found", then a 5-hop chain; 6 false callers removed (stricter 2 of 7 before and after) |
| 30 | `f.call()` and `f.apply()` are calls | fastify-14 | incomplete, then complete (both methods) |
| 30 | function-local Go/Rust/GDScript declarations are not symbols | 28 fzf and nfpm cells; 574 symbols removed on fzf, gotestsum, nfpm | stricter 12 before and 12 after: fzf-12 incomplete to complete, fzf-02 complete to incomplete (its old credit rested on a call edge to a function-local `var`) |
| 30 | `--for` tail rows name their file's top symbols | 120 `--for` cells | stricter 41, then 43 (fastify-13, starlette-11); more lenient 88, then 89; none lower; +1.2 KB per answer on average |
| 30 | `--path` hops read `Owner.method` | 16 `--path` cells | none lower; flake8-14 matched 1 of its items, then 4 |
| 30 | a call's result type types the next receiver (Go, Rust, Java, Kotlin, TypeScript) | 8 target cells (nfpm, mdBook); a census on nushell and envoy | no cell moved; the binding of 880 call sites on nushell (Rust) and 76 on envoy (Go, Rust, Kotlin) changed, 16 nushell sites checked by hand, 0 false |
| 31 | `--for` appends the bodies of its top ranked rows | 53 `--for` rows | stricter +4 (hono-02, hono-11, koa-02, textual-02), none lost; the whole answer grows by 3.4 KB median |
| 31 | a callers list is served whole while its rows fit 16,000 B | tmux-07 `--callers=options_get_number` | 40 of 121 callers, then 121 of 121, in one call (4,604 to 11,434 B) |
| 31 | a qualified annotation proves a class only through an in-tree qualifier | 62,750 call sites on six repositories | 0 change: an honesty fix that no measured row needed |
| 31 | `--for`'s first eight rows name eight files; a `.d.ts` ranks below its implementation | 44 rows | stricter 27, then 29 (fastify-11, fastify-13, from the `.d.ts` rule); more lenient 39 before and after; files named in the first 8 rows 3.96, then 8.00 on average |
| 31 | `--path` names what an unreached path stopped at and offers a hedged bridge; `--callees` lists closures | the 54 hardest rows | stricter 1, then 3 (htop-14, nunjucks-21); more lenient 24, then 26; none lower; 0 wrong hits (textual-11 from refused to partial) |

## What got better, in words
- **Complete answers.** `--for` stops when it is complete, opens one owner body for a "how does X work" question, appends bodies and names more files; `--callers` and `--callees` serve up to 50 rows whole; `--impact` of a type reaches the files that use it; the calls the resolver declined are listed as hedged `<dc>` rows instead of being counted and dropped; `--grep` names who reads a constant.
- **Fewer false edges.** Go methods carry their receiver type; a local bound to a call takes the callee's declared result type; a Rust call named like a standard collection member binds no in-tree namesake; a TypeScript or Python annotation `q.T` proves a class only through an in-tree `q`; `x op= v` rebinds; Ruby and Python `x[k]` is a call only where the receiver is proven.
- **Hedged instead of silent.** `--safe-delete` reads `risk="hedged"` for a method `getattr(obj, f"watch_{name}")` or `this['compile' + x]` can reach; a multi-definition answer says which definition each row belongs to.
- **Memory and safety.** `--quality-delta=A..B` holds one commit's index at a time (a 20,356-file repository's `HEAD~1..HEAD` had been killed at an 8 GiB limit, #387); on Linux the guard counts the cgroup's real charge, not just the resident set.
- **Markdown.** A link `[text](other.md#slug)` edges to that heading instead of the file, and a link no call shares is marked `via="link"` (@muayyad-alsadi, #409, #414).
- **Languages.** Clojure (`.clj`, `.cljs`, `.cljc`, `.bb`; #349) parsed 4,930 of 4,933 files from four public checkouts; that is parser completion, not call-resolution accuracy. Elixir `unquote(...)` calls are calls again (#357, #380).
- **Faster.** `--pr-context=HEAD~30` on this repository: 49.45 s and 45.79 s became 8.66 s and 7.67 s (two interleaved runs each, output byte-identical). The startup git check no longer spawns a `git rev-parse` (269 to 351 ms in our four-repository measurement).

## What did not move, and what it cost
- Answers are larger: +19.9% on the 60 development questions above; the body fold adds 3.4 KB median to a `--for` answer; in the callers-band change's sweep, 89 of 158 answers changed, by a median of +3,357 B.
- One change aimed at five rows and flipped one (rake-02; the bar was four). Two of the three rows built for the owner body flipped (fastify-12, ninja-11); koa-12 did not.
- C++ and Objective-C call results are not typed yet: a macro can declare a name no reader sees. Rust receivers written as an in-tree type are declined and counted, not bound (5 true mdBook edges declined, 72 false claims removed).

## Thanks
Code: @LaimaWu (#380 Elixir `unquote`, #382 Python imports on shared captures), @mpapis (#396, #401, #412: Ruby mixins and the Rails/DSL work on the shared path; slice 4a, #400), @tonibergholm-codento (#387 report, #391 and #392: the memory fixes) and @tag-und-nacht (#349, Clojure).
Ideas and reports: @muayyad-alsadi (#409, markdown as a graph; code in #414, links that bind the exact heading), whose work also inspired the HTML help-wanted issue #417 (slices you can claim). Other help-wanted slices are listed in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, which now says where Rust, C++ and Go need the most help.
Open pull requests we have not merged yet: #397 (@pt-act), #402, #410 and #411 (@lennix1337). Thank you.

## Versions and caches
Parser version 206, cache version 36, quality-snapshot scheme 22; the legend dictionary is `dictv=30173b0aa2d06473 entries=908`. Caches written by 0.6.7 or any earlier build are rebuilt once.

Full notes: [CHANGELOG.md, section 0.6.8](https://github.com/redhat-et/ripwire/blob/v0.6.8/CHANGELOG.md).

name: Niubash v1.4.2
body:
Niubash v1.4.2 packages for Windows, Linux, and macOS.

Engine: rubash git a83a09d32b4a — every platform build in this release compiled that same revision, pinned by `scripts/release/rubash-pin.json` and fail-hard verified at fetch time (rubash#827). The release compiles the pinned engine, not "whatever rubash master was when the pipeline ran".
Verify locally with `niu --version`, which prints the same revision.

Windows (x64, ARM64): Inno Setup installers (`*-setup.exe`) add user PATH and Windows Terminal profile integration; portable zips bundle `niu` with WinuxCmd and bash/sh shims.

Windows packages come with the must-install bundle pre-installed (niubash#189, niubash#209): niugit (native Windows git — the full plugin distro's five entries install through git, so a fresh machine without git.exe no longer fails `niu setup`), gawk 5.4.1 with plain `awk` working too, plus ripgrep (`rg`) and fd — all landing in the bundled WinuxCmd root as wpm JSON-package payloads, assembled at CI time with no runtime downloads, no archive formats beyond the release zip itself, and no symlinks. Pre-install is best-effort, not a promise: on legs where the package index has no matching artifact (currently niugit and gawk on the ARM64 builds; ripgrep and fd have ARM64 artifacts) the package ships WITHOUT that entry — run `winuxcmd wpm install <name>` once after installing to add it. The pre-install list and its recorded exclusions live in `scripts/release/preinstall.json`.

`niubash-skill-v<version>.zip` is the AI agent skill bundle (SKILL.md + references, WinuxCmd-skill layout): unpack it into an agent skills directory, or let the shell do it — `niu skill install` embeds the same content.

Linux (x86_64, aarch64; glibc): portable tarballs with the `niu` binary, README, and LICENSE — Unix builds bundle nothing, native system tools are used. Untar anywhere and run `./niu`.

macOS (aarch64, x86_64): portable tarballs with the `niu` binary, README, and LICENSE. Untar anywhere and run `./niu`.

Every artifact was smoke-verified on the build OS of the job that produced it, before upload: `niu -c 'echo ok'`, `printf 'a\nb\n' | niu -c 'sort | head -1'`, an offline `NIU_PLUGIN_SPEC=<empty> niu plugin sync --bootstrap` (exit 0, no output, no network), and a `niu --version` check against this tag and the engine revision.

Integrity (niubash#311): `SHA256SUMS` lists the SHA-256 of every shipped artifact, and each Windows installer has a `.sha256` sidecar beside it. `niu --self-update` verifies the installer against the sidecar before running it and aborts rather than execute anything it cannot verify. The same digests feed the winget manifest `InstallerSha256`.


## What's Changed
* fix(unix): discover the installed shell by platform binary name by @caomengxuan666 in https://github.com/unixwin/niubash/pull/463
* fix(login): report login_shell shopt as on for argv[0]-marked login shells by @caomengxuan666 in https://github.com/unixwin/niubash/pull/465


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/unixwin/niubash/compare/v1.4.1...v1.4.2

## Verifying GitHub Artifact Attestations

The artifacts in this release have attestations generated with GitHub Artifact Attestations. These can be verified by using the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify):
```sh
gh attestation verify <file-path of downloaded artifact> --repo astral-sh/uv
```

You can also download the attestation from [GitHub](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/attestations) and verify against that directly:
```sh
gh attestation verify <file-path of downloaded artifact> --bundle <file-path of downloaded attestation>
```

## Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-19.

### Enhancements

- Report all installed packages in `uv workspace metadata`, including packages outside the selected resolution ([#22395](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22395))
- Include supported environment restrictions when exporting `pylock.toml` ([#22596](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22596))
- Retry dropped GET and HEAD requests when fetching package and index data ([#22672](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22672))
- Preserve encoding declarations in wheel data scripts that require shell launchers ([#22526](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22526))
- Show causes and hints when `uv python find --script` cannot discover an interpreter, including with `-q` ([#22549](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22549))
- Print valid ksh activation instructions and support non-relocatable environments under OpenBSD-derived ksh ([#22538](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22538), [#22572](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22572))
- Allow PEP 508 direct URLs, including Mercurial and extensionless archive URLs, in uv-build's `[build-system].requires` validation ([#22577](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22577))

### Python

- Add PyPy 3.11.17 and 3.12.15 ([#22578](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22578))

### Preview features

- Fetch and parse PEP 825 index-level variant metadata with `wheel-variants` ([#22509](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22509), [#22511](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22511))

### Performance

- Avoid exponential work when simplifying, traversing, and exporting complex dependency markers ([#22608](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22608), [#22615](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22615), [#22651](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22651), [#22674](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22674))
- Reduce the time and memory used to parse and store complex dependency markers ([#22675](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22675), [#22676](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22676), [#22681](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22681))
- Reduce resolver memory use for large dependency graphs, forks, extras, and dependency groups ([#22565](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22565), [#22625](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22625))
- Speed up project discovery in large workspaces by caching member names ([#22635](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22635))
- Reduce uv's binary size and speed up CycloneDX exports ([#22431](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22431))
- Reduce `uv-build` binary size, including Linux x86_64 wheels ([#22539](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22539), [#22573](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22573))
- Reduce allocations when parsing TOML ([#22679](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22679))

### Bug fixes

- Respect `--exclude-newer` when a newer wheel for the selected source distribution is already cached ([#22685](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22685))
- Prevent URL credentials from leaking through diagnostics or persisted metadata ([#22600](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22600), [#22601](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22601), [#22617](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22617), [#22622](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22622), [#22646](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22646))
- Keep separate cache entries for signed `--find-links` URLs that differ only in sensitive query values ([#22630](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22630))
- Honor PEP 751 environment restrictions when installing or syncing from `pylock.toml` ([#22594](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22594))
- Use configured credentials before prompting during `uv publish`, and avoid prompting when no upload occurs ([#22593](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22593))
- Match recursive build globs against complete file paths and ignore invalid license symlinks ([#22581](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22581), [#22583](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22583))
- Return an error for invalid `uv pip compile --python-version` values instead of panicking ([#22727](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22727))
- Reject invalid `pylock.toml` output filenames before resolution instead of panicking ([#22725](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22725))
- Avoid panicking during repeated resolution conflicts involving fixed-priority packages ([#22589](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22589))
- Create version aliases correctly when installing managed Python into a relative directory ([#22547](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22547))
- Show incompatibilities from failing `uv pip check` invocations with `-q` ([#22544](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22544))
- Treat logically equivalent dependency markers as equal regardless of construction order ([#22680](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22680))

### Rust API

- Require the opt-in `unsafe-url` feature to use raw `url::Url` APIs in `uv-pep508` ([#22623](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22623))

### Documentation

- Clarify credential lookup, environment synchronization, managed Python, and integration guidance ([#22542](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22542))

### Other changes

- Use stable `sh.astral.*` signing identifiers for macOS binaries ([#22648](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/22648))

## Install uv 0.13.2

### Install prebuilt binaries via shell script

```sh
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://releases.astral.sh/github/uv/releases/download/0.13.2/uv-installer.sh | sh
```

name: v0.5.1.1
body:
## 中文

修复 v0.5.1 中后续 session commit 生成的记忆无法检索的问题：第一次 session commit 正常，但继续 add message 后再次 commit，会出现任务显示完成、新增记忆却无法通过 `find` 或 `search` 检索的情况。升级后，后续 commit 生成的记忆可以正常建立索引并被检索。([#6331](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/pull/6331))

## English

Fixes a v0.5.1 bug where the first session commit produced searchable memories, but later commits after adding more messages could report completion while newly generated memories were missing from `find` and `search`. Memories generated by subsequent commits are now indexed and searchable. ([#6331](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/pull/6331))

[Full Changelog / 完整变更](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/compare/v0.5.1...v0.5.1.1)

name: Skill 4.7.0
body:
- **Critique and audit desktop apps.** Start an Electron, NW.js, CEF or WebView2 app with a debugging port and `impeccable detect --cdp 9222` scans the window you have open, as it stands, and leaves it exactly as it found it. Critique and audit know the recipe.

- **Two new typography checks.** `straggler` catches a paragraph that ends on one lonely word, and `unbalanced-heading` a heading whose last line is a stub. `text-wrap: balance` and `pretty` stand them down where they fix the problem.

- **Fewer false alarms on real pages.** Labels that look like buttons, card numbers, code samples that scroll, text behind curtain footers and pass-through overlays, light copy on a dark halo, and frosted glass now read the way a visitor sees them. Border accents are judged per selector, not by how many blank lines sit nearby.

- **A lighter skill.** The description that loads into every session is 30% shorter, and it now picks up requests to write a DESIGN.md or document a design system. Older command files lost their shouted CRITICAL and NEVER banners, and polish passes are no longer cut off after two rounds outside a full build.

- **Review pages follow dark mode.** The decision and review pages match your OS appearance, while comps and captures keep their own backgrounds.

- **Monorepos pick the right app.** `context` offers only workspaces that render a UI as targets, not tsconfig, lint or script packages.

- **Fixes.** Live mode starts on a LAN or Tailscale address over plain HTTP. Decision cards render in WebKit in-app browsers, and no longer get stuck on pending when the page loads many images at once. Discarding a variant whose wrapper lost its original no longer deletes the element. An interrupted engine download cleans up after itself, on Windows too.

name: impeccable engine engine-v0.1.16
body: Prebuilt impeccable engine binaries (engine-v0.1.16). The launcher, the npm shim and impeccable install download these on first run. Docs: https://impeccable.style

name: CLI 4.7.0
body:
- **Desktop and webview apps.** Point `--cdp` at a local debugging port, and use `--target` to pick a window when there are several. 
`npx impeccable@latest detect --cdp 9222 --target "My App"`
- **The current detector.** Engine 0.1.16 brings the new typography checks and every accuracy fix in skill v4.7.0.

name: Cua Spaces v0.11.0
body:
## Cua Spaces 0.11.0

### New
- **Resources at a glance.** Home, each computer's page and the menu bar now show processor, memory and disk use.
- **Prompts for This Mac.** Cua asks before a second agent connects, and before an agent does something risky.
- **One first run everywhere.** Connect your agent, and This Mac is your first Space.
- **Self-hosting** now lives under Settings > Advanced.

### Better
- Setup starts with your computer's name already filled in, and every option says in everyday words what it does.
- The Done screen is honest: it notices the CLI and sign-in you already have.
- Usage is counted in "remote hours" everywhere you see it.
- Wording says "computer" instead of "machine".
- Optional usage data can link to your account, but stays off until our policy is published.

### Fixed
- Sharing a Linux remote desktop asks for the password, says what to do when it can't share, and explains why a share failed.
- Moving an app session between computers now carries only the items you pick.

name: cua-driver-rs: v0.37.0
body:
# Cua Driver 0.37.0

## Summary

This release adds 5 features and includes 17 fixes.

## Features

- add browser_select for native HTML select. ([#5232](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5232))
- let agents approve Cua Driver's macOS prompts when the owner authorizes it. ([#5467](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5467))
- recovery hints on refusals and unverifiable results. ([#5493](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5493))
- install the skill pack when setting up an agent, and add get_guide. ([#5491](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5491))
- optional brief foreground step for native drag-and-drop on macOS. ([#5481](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5481))

## Fixes

- list untitled X11 windows the window manager manages. ([#5341](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5341)) Thanks @abonneth.
- ask for macOS's direct-capture consent during setup, not over the user's window (CUA-1792). ([#5352](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5352))
- don't open a background web <select>; steer to set_value (CUA-1795). ([#5353](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5353))
- install Antigravity skills in IDE and CLI directories. ([#5226](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5226)) Thanks @Kenmege.
- verify macOS target focus before dispatching keys. ([#5372](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5372)) Thanks @fynixart.
- derive the macOS desktop point ratio from the display mode instead of a screenshot. ([#5340](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5340)) Thanks @abonneth.
- keep rendered controls visible in semantic_v2 and report not_rendered for background tabs. ([#5256](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5256))
- deliver background drags in Electron windows through the main process (CUA-1207). ([#5351](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5351))
- count a bundle-identifier capture approval as consent (fixes hosted macOS preflight). ([#5402](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5402))
- leave focus on a dialog the clicked app opened. ([#5258](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5258)) Thanks @CMGS.
- uninstall keeps macOS permissions unless asked; release gate pins the app signing requirement. ([#5460](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5460))
- report a locked screen and keep the display awake while an agent works. ([#5483](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5483))
- match path-style app grants against the full executable path. ([#5505](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5505))
- keep the pointer out of macOS window screenshots. ([#5480](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5480))
- launch the installed app by path, stop daemons from any copy, drop extra copies. ([#5471](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5471))
- let the client wait out the largest tool budget. ([#5526](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5526)) Thanks @abonneth.
- refuse background menus bound to sibling windows. ([#5520](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5520)) Thanks @saariuslystoned.

## Performance

- read macOS bundle plists in process. ([#5369](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5369)) Thanks @hqhq1025.
- faster batched steps and window reads, and a nudge to batch. ([#5487](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5487))

## Contributors

Thanks to @abonneth, @CMGS, @fynixart, @hqhq1025, @Kenmege, @saariuslystoned for contributing to this release.

## Install

macOS and Linux:

```bash
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh)"
```

Windows:

```powershell
irm https://cua.ai/driver/install.ps1 | iex
```

Cua Driver ships universal macOS binaries, x86_64 and arm64 Windows builds,
and Linux preview builds. Release assets also include tag-pinned installer and
uninstaller scripts.

## Why GitHub says “Pre-release”

GitHub's label is used only to keep this monorepo's repository-wide “Latest”
pointer from switching between independently released products. A plain Cua
Driver SemVer is a stable release; npm and PyPI publish it on
their normal stable channels, and the installers resolve the versioned
`cua-driver-rs-v*` releases directly.
